description:
YOU CAN RUN OUT OF A STUMBLE. ONE BYTE. This is the other half of the complaint - the half where you have LOST the ball. Test it SECOND, alone, after contact-dribble-cancel-early.json.

THE PROBLEM. There are two locks stacked on each other and this pack is aimed at the bigger one. Before any timing gate is consulted, each action asks 'may I start at all, given what this player is currently doing?' - that is vtable slot 2, canStart. While the current action is a Stagger, plain locomotion is refused OUTRIGHT. Not 'refused for now' - refused at every frame, forever, until the stagger ends by itself. Emulated at frame 120, long past every cancel key: Move is still dropped. Waiting does not help, because nothing is waiting; the request is thrown away one layer above the timer. That is literally 'I hold the stick and nothing happens', and it is why being tackled off the ball feels like a cutscene rather than a contest.

WHAT CHANGES. match::anime::action::Move::vf2 (0x143f688c0) is a compare chain, not a jump table:
    sub ecx,3      je -> ALLOW          (current kind 3)
    sub ecx,0x53   je -> ALLOW          (current kind 0x56, DemoMove)
    sub ecx,7      je -> ASK the gate   (current kind 0x5d, InplayDemoKickFailed)
    sub ecx,1      je -> ASK the gate   (current kind 0x5e, InplayDemoFatigueInjury)
    cmp ecx,1      je -> ASK the gate   (current kind 0x5f, InplayDemoMove)
    xor al,al      -> REFUSE everything else, including Stagger 0x10 and FallDown 0x11
At the third line ecx holds currentKind - 0x56. This pack changes that one imm8 from 7 to 0xBA, i.e. 'sub ecx,7' becomes 'sub ecx,-0x46', so ecx becomes currentKind - 0x10 and the three delegate slots slide from current kinds 0x5d/0x5e/0x5f onto 0x10/0x11/0x12 - Stagger, FallDown and Feint. One byte, same instruction length, no cell written, no new code.

MEASURED EFFECT (a-EMULATED, this pass, end to end through the REAL requester 0x143eb4f40):
    request Move while...     stock       THIS PACK
    ... in a Stagger          never       opens at the first cancel key (frame 16 in the test layout)
    ... in a FallDown         never       opens at the LAST cancel key  (frame 48 in the test layout)
    ... in a Dive             never       never (unchanged - Dive is refused by a different entry)
'never' means dropped at every frame from 0 to 199, which is the stock behaviour and is the thing being complained about.

HOW IT KEEPS THE WEIGHT. It does not allow Move outright - it routes Move to the SAME cancel gate every other action already asks. The stagger still plays, still has to reach its first cancel keyframe, and still costs you that time. What changes is that at the end of it you are running instead of standing. Note the FallDown row is deliberately the LATE gate: being put on the floor still costs a full animation, which is the weight you asked for when you asked for more falls.

THE PRICE, STATED PLAINLY. Move loses the ability to interrupt the three in-play demo reactions. Two of the three cost nothing: InplayDemoKickFailed (0x5d) and InplayDemoFatigueInjury (0x5e) both inherit the base vf14 stub at 0x140c853c0 ('xor al,al; ret' = never interruptible), verified in their vtables this pass, so those delegate slots were already dead ends. Only InplayDemoMove (0x5f) has a live vf14 (0x143fb8630) and genuinely loses the interrupt. Watch for a player stuck jogging through an in-play demo cutaway. That is the entire cost.

EVIDENCE.
  a-EMULATED - Move::vf2 and the full request chain on the game's own bytes: 0x143eb4f40 -> Move::vf2 0x143f688c0 -> Stagger::vf14 0x143f00de0 -> starter 0x143eb4fd0. Harness tools/emu_contact_request.py, output build/emu_contact_request_proof.txt sections 1, 3, 4 and 7.
  a-EMULATED - the requester is real: 0x143eb4fad 'mov rcx,[rax] / mov r8,[rcx+0x10] / mov rcx,rax / call r8 / test al,al / jne -> call 0x143eb4fd0'. Slot 2 is offset 0x10. Earlier passes could not find this and correctly refused to claim the lever would work; it is now demonstrated.
  b-DISASSEMBLY - the Move::vf2 compare chain at 0x143f688d2..0x143f688e9, read instruction by instruction.
  b-DISASSEMBLY - the two dead demo slots, from the InplayDemoKickFailed / InplayDemoFatigueInjury vtables.
  NOT CLAIMED - that 0x143eb4f40 is the ONLY path a held direction can take. It is one gated requester and it has a single caller (0x143f0c615); other code calls the starter 0x143eb4fd0 directly for internal transitions. If a human's locomotion is driven by one of those ungated paths instead, this pack does nothing at all. The failure mode is NO EFFECT, not a bad effect.

WHO IT AFFECTS: EVERYONE. Move::vf2 has no cursor test and no human/CPU discriminator. CPU players will also chase out of stumbles.

WHAT YOU SHOULD SEE IN ONE MATCH. Get tackled so the ball runs loose a couple of yards. Stock you watch the stumble and the ball is gone. With this you should be able to push the stick and go after it while still stumbling out of the contact.

WHAT WOULD FALSIFY IT. Absolutely no difference in two halves. That is the documented risk above - it would mean human locomotion does not travel through this requester. Do not stack something else on top to 'make it work'; report the null result, because it is a real finding.

WHAT WOULD MEAN IT IS TOO FAR. Players pivoting and sprinting out of heavy collisions with no stumble step at all, or an in-play demo where a player keeps jogging through the cutaway.

COLLISIONS. Site 0x143f688de verified byte-identical between the INSTALLED image and eFootball.exe.PRISTINE this pass (both 07). No overlap with any applied spec. Independent of contact-dribble-cancel-early.json (different function, different request kind) - but apply them on separate outings anyway, because both move the same felt quantity.

EXPECTED EFFECT ON FOULS AND CARDS: none directly. It adds no challenge; it only lets a stumbling player relocate.

REVERT: python tools/exe_patch.py remove tools/data/patches/contact-move-out-of-stagger.json

patches.name: Move::vf2 delegate window re-aimed from the in-play demos to Stagger/FallDown/Feint
patches.note: 'sub ecx,7' -> 'sub ecx,-0x46' (imm8 07 -> BA, sign-extended) inside match::anime::action::Move::vf2 (0x143f688c0). At this point ecx = currentKind - 0x56, so after the edit ecx = currentKind - 0x10 and the three following delegate branches match current kinds 0x10 (Stagger), 0x11 (FallDown) and 0x12 (Feint) instead of 0x5d/0x5e/0x5f (the in-play demo reactions). Same instruction length, no pool cell involved.
